tagline: India's water-transport pioneer — the Kochi Water Metro is the country's first integrated electric ferry network across the backwaters.
summary: Kochi (Cochin) is built across a cluster of islands in the Vembanad backwaters on Kerala's coast. The Kochi Water Metro, run by KMRL, is India's first integrated urban water-transport system — battery-electric boats linking ten islands to the Ernakulam mainland and the Kochi Metro rail on a single ticket, with the network expanding toward 38 terminals and 16 routes. Every backwater leg is sheltered and well inside Pioneer II range, making Kochi a standout public-transport waterway market with an all-electric mandate already in place.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II covers the entire Kochi Water Metro network — every backwater line from High Court to Kakkanad and Vypin is sheltered and well inside the 70nm range.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) could extend to wider Kerala backwater trunks (Alappuzha/Kottayam) beyond the Kochi network.

competitive_landscape: KMRL runs the all-electric Kochi Water Metro. Navier is a passenger-only foiling layer above the existing service, covering the same routes far faster while extending Kochi's electric water-transport model.
regulatory_note: Low-wake operation through the shallow Vembanad backwaters and busy local-ferry jetties; foiling only where the dredged Water Metro channels allow.
